tweets.text:
Walter Russell Mead (@wrmead) on why tech companies are starting to demand their employees be patriotic:

"Increasingly, companies are starting to realize that they need their employees to be patriotic. 

That is, your employees need to think it's an evil sin to sell IP to China. 

And that your coworkers will rat you out in a heartbeat if they think you're doing something like that."

"One of the biggest things that happened in modern American history is the mutual discovery of tech and government. 

In the 1990s, companies would say, I'm not an American company, I'm a global company, and nowhere was that stronger than in the world of tech, where Google has no boundaries.

Today, tech is actually the locus of international great power competition. 

China's attempt to build a technosphere that can dominate the American technosphere is critical to your business, but also to the American state, to power and independence. 

So much to the surprise of both the tech world and the political world, they've been driven in on each other, and there's a kind of re-nationalization of tech.

If you're a legacy multinational, free trade is the essence of your business. I need financial markets, labor markets, and manufactured good markets that are seamless and open. 

But if you're a tech company, you don't. Google is not importing and exporting a lot of goods. 

You're much more concerned about security of supply chain, security of intellectual property."

tweets.text:
Walter Russell Mead (@wrmead) on Donald Trump:

"He's discovered one of the secrets of power in the contemporary world, which is he's managed to turn fame into power, drama into power, and to do it in ways that leave him completely free to act. 

If you lie enough, the marginal cost of your 10,000th lie is nothing, while the marginal cost of your first, second, or third lie is very high. 

So all of the normal constraints on political figures, reputational and so on, he does not pay."

"The Donald Trump show is the most compelling entertainment, infotainment spectacle that humanity has ever seen. 

Since the dawn of time, no living human being has occupied the amount of bandwidth of the human race that Donald Trump does. And he sees that as the key to his unique power.

He is a major historic figure who has developed a new understanding of how power works in an era of mass communications and social media, and the rest of us are just trying to deal with it."

The growth pace on Robinhood's chain is unreal.

In around 2 months:

→ TVL went from $42.3M to $783M (1,750%)
→ Stablecoin supply went from $241M to $868M (260%)
→ Daily DEX volume went from $32.4M to $1.55B (4,680%)

Pretty ridiculous numbers for such a short time.

Also, DEX volume grew much faster than TVL, which tells you the growth is coming from heavy trading, not just people depositing more capital.

Again, this is a big result of Robinhood being established in this space. It already had millions of users, wallets, stock tokens, stablecoins, and partners before the chain's launch.

The memecoin rally will be the main thing we remember it by going forward, though.

tweets.text:
I spent much of the weekend talking with the team who did this work. Seb--and everyone else--acted with integrity and generosity throughout.

Initially we believed the other team had also solved the problem. We wanted to collaborate and do a joint release. 

When we learned that they had Euler but not Navier-Stokes, we offered to let them go first, to suggest that they should be the ones to get the prize, and optionally for Tristan to be the lead author on a rewrite of the OpenAI proof. We felt it was challenging to offer the same to Levent (an Anthropic employee), who was not willing to talk or coordinate with us anyway. We were open to other solutions.

We would have greatly preferred coordination. We did not rush to publish even though the other team wasn't communicating with us. The team threatened us with unfounded accusations of plagarism.

Now that we can see their work, the approaches appear to be different. It is also worth noting that our latest model can solve many, many other math problems.

It is true that we tried this because there were rumors on the internet last week that Anthropic's models had solved a millennium problem and we were curious if ours could do it too.
tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
I would like to clarify a few things:

1) The screenshot is my reaching out to Levent to coordinate our releases. I hope it’s clear from the message that we came in with the best possible intentions.

2) I never ever asked for Levent to be removed from authorship of his own work https://t.co/yRli0hLNuM

@Jason:

“They're basically hijacking the media with this performative framing of the AI being sentient.

And if you just call this software and software testing, and use the classic language like bugs, audit log, then it would never have made its way into the media.

And when the media gets their hooks into this, having been a journalist and having watched journalism move from being a truth-seeking function in society, and then become an entertainment vehicle in society where any chance you get to increase your ratings, that's the problem.

Because now what Dwarkesh has done, and I don't think Dwarkesh has bad intentions here, I think he wrote something because he wanted to get attention for his point of view, but you give that to the media, the media's like, ‘This is going to get us ratings. This is going to get us clicks. This is going to get us advertising.’

So they're more than willing to engage in this farcical act and this dance with Anthropic and OpenAI and then just publicize it.

So all the free clicks, we call this earned media in the space, you didn't have to pay for it, now OpenAI got so much earned media before their IPO and Dwarkesh just absolutely put kerosene on that fire, and it made its way to the national press.

That story has now gotten everywhere. It's priming the pump to buy the IPO shares. It's ridiculous.”

You work your ass off to get a lot of money. But what is that money actually for?

Money has no intrinsic value—it only matters if you have a clear purpose behind it. Will it get you better friends, a better marriage, or a better relationship with your kids? You better answer that question first.

To me, real success isn’t about the money. Success is knowing your nature, finding the best path through that nature, and being able to look back and say, "That was the life I wanted to have."

Credit: Sam Parr, Shaan Puri, and My First Million

#RayDalio #DefinitionOfSuccess #MoneyAndPurpose #Mindset

I have a t-shirt that says Decentralize Everything. That is 40 years of observation compressed into two words, and I finally wrote the argument down as the first guest contributor to @CryptoniteRap.

The piece is about DeSci, decentralized science.

Every institution stagnates the same way. A small group ends up controlling the agenda, that group gets invested in the current framework, and challenging the consensus becomes a career risk. I have watched it in banking, telecom, rocketry, and now science.

After 40 years I boiled it down to two rules.

1- The Draper Equation: the likelihood that a society needs to rethink an industry is proportional to the number of people benefiting from existing theories without change.

2- The Draper Corollary: the more centralized the decision-making, the less innovation occurs. The more decentralized the operations, the more innovation occurs and the faster that sector grows.

The consensus mocked Hotmail, Skype, Tesla, Bitcoin, and SpaceX too. Every time, mockery was an excellent signal.

Read the full editorial: https://t.co/kMYEnjkQTc

tweets.text:
some thoughts on this

1/ first off must read, good compilation of projects ; really good alpha gathering here

2/ secondly from markets perspective i find that lending & borrowing is a very much solved primitive and as such new protocols dont really have much moat especially when entrenched winners move over. i mean lending, borrowing, yield - not only are these verticals solved, they're also sorely based on antifragility - w all the hacks going on, no one wants to put serious money into a protocol 2 weeks old. 

theres also no real new innovation to be done here; hence no new earnings inflection on top of existing defi revenue. 

3/ as such i dont really view lending borrowing tokens net new nor interesting

4/ dex tokens and launchpads are the obvious longs here when a chain picks up. this trade is evidently late with the top launchpad up 100x ; but i think there is space for a winning dex / aggregator - we've found the pump of RH, but the raydium / jupiter is yet to be seen. 

with uniswap on the chain though, i think an aggregator makes alot more sense than a standalone dex. 

5/ stock token pairs are very much memes - i dont think theres any new innovative layers here. at best i believe these will trade like beta to the underlying, at worst i dont see a key differential bw token1 paired to stockXYZ and token2 paired to the same stock. 

and so the framework to approach this is w akin to memes - all an attention game

6/ taking all this into consideration, to me, there is at best 5 tokens to long on RH chain - personally only like 2 ; bear in mind i am not a meme guy (bad at these games)

7/ side note - alts at these levels feels like do or die - we had the mania, we had the celebrity coins, we have all the grifters coming out of the woodwork aft 1 day. 

i will say, if we only get 1-2 weeks of pump though, that would be very disappointing, even for crypto

sometimes you just have to take a chance
